title: Standardization of TIN in Regulatory Compliance
summary: The Tax Identification Number (TIN) evolved from a basic requirement for customs licensing into a standardized, mandatory data point across various regulatory instruments. Over time, the focus shifted from simple submission to the requirement of 'updated' TINs in formal affidavits, reflecting a move toward more rigorous, system-based audit and verification processes.

evolution.scope: Expanded from simple licensing to include factory inspections, audit identification, and foreign director compliance.
evolution.procedure: Transitioned from static document submission to mandatory 'updated' status reporting in formal affidavits.

timeline.change: Initial requirement for e-TIN certificate for customs agent licensing.
Integration of TIN into factory inspection reports for concessional import benefits.
TIN established as a primary identifier for system-based audit and transaction retrieval.
Mandatory TIN submission for foreign directors regardless of residency status.
Requirement for 'updated' TIN in formal firm profile affidavits.

National Board of Revenue: The licensing authority must obtain permission from the Board before initiating the customs agent licensing process.
The Board has the power to grant an extension of time for the licensing authority to issue a license if it fails to meet the initial deadline.
Customs Act 1969: Applicants must demonstrate practical knowledge of the Customs Act 1969, among other relevant laws, as part of the licensing requirements.
Tax Identification Number: An applicant is required to submit a valid electronic Taxpayer Identification Number certificate as part of the mandatory documentation for a customs agent license.
Partnership Act 1932: If an applicant is a partnership firm, they must submit a certified copy of the partnership deed as required by the Partnership Act 1932.
Customs Agent License: The licensing authority follows a structured procedure including application submission, document verification, examination, and fee payment to issue a license.
Applicants must provide proof of professional qualifications, financial solvency, and various corporate or personal legal documents to be eligible for the license.
The licensing authority may reject an application for valid reasons, providing written notice to the applicant within a specified timeframe.

উপযুক্তৃ তথ্যারদ পযাৃলোচনায় প্রতীয়মান হয় রয, বরণতৃ প্ররতষ্ঠানটি স্থানীয়ভ্ালব বপ্র-মফবিদকদটড বববডাং স্ট্রাকচার উৎপাদলনি লদক্ষয প্রাথরমক প্রস্তুরত িম্পন্ন করিয়ালে। প্ররতষ্ঠানটিকে প্রজ্ঞাপন এস.আর.ও. নং ১৯৩-আইন/২০২৪/৪৫/কাস্টমি, তারিখ: ২৯ মম, ২০২৪ রিষ্টাব্দ এি আওতায় প্রজ্ঞাপলন উরিরখত পণ্য/যন্ত্াাংি/উপকিণ রিয়ারত সুরবধায় আমদারনি অনুলমাদন প্রদালনি সুপারিি কিা হইে।

জাতীয় িাজস্ব রবালিিৃ প্ররতরনরধি নাম ও স্বাক্ষি
তারিখ:

Business Identification Number: The factory inspection report requires the submission of the Business Identification Number to verify the tax compliance status of the manufacturing facility.
Tax Identification Number: The factory inspection report requires the Tax Identification Number of the owner or proprietor as part of the official documentation for factory assessment.
S.R.O. 193-AIN/2024: This notification establishes the regulatory framework under which the manufacturing facility is recommended for the import of goods, machinery, or components at concessional rates.
The inspection report serves as the basis for granting import privileges to a facility that has completed the necessary preparations for producing prefabricated building structures.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is one of the designated authorities responsible for signing the factory inspection report to validate the eligibility of the entity for fiscal benefits.
